name: Smurf Cat (Шайлушай)
blurb: A blue, cat-like Smurf from 2014 concept art that became a TikTok meme in August 2023
aka: We Live We Love We Lie
title: Smurf Cat Meme: Meaning, Origin & "We Live, We Love, We Lie"
description: Smurf Cat (Шайлушай) uses Nate Hallinan's "Smurf Sighting" art; it took off on TikTok in August 2023 with Alan Walker's "The Spectre".
h1: What is the Smurf Cat meme?
answer: Smurf Cat is a meme of a realistic blue creature in a white Smurf hat that many viewers read as a cat. The picture is "Smurf Sighting", concept art by artist Nate Hallinan published in 2014. On 26–27 August 2023 a Russian-speaking TikToker began posting slideshows of it, named it "Шайлушай" (Shailushai) and set it to a remix of Alan Walker's "The Spectre", whose lyric "we live, we love, we lie" gave the meme its other name.

body: The image is a lifelike, blue-skinned Smurf in its white hat. Its face looks feline and the hat looks a bit like a mushroom, so people call it Smurf Cat or Blue Mushroom Cat. In memes it is dropped into everyday scenes in photo slideshows, with "шайлушай" written over it in white Impact text.

body.note: The artwork is by concept artist Nate Hallinan, who shared progress shots in September 2011 and published the finished piece on his website on 9 September 2014. Memes use recoloured and edited versions of it. "Шайлушай" is gibberish in Russian, though it sounds like "шалопай", a playful word for a little rascal.

head: Date
Event
rows: Nate Hallinan publishes the "Smurf Sighting" artwork on his website.
TikToker @ghojam1 posts the first slideshow of the creature; it gets about 900,000 plays in five days.
A second slideshow names it "шайлушай" and uses the "The Spectre" remix; it passes 2 million plays in four days.
The hashtag passes 8 million views and the meme jumps from Russian-language TikTok to the wider internet.
A "Шайлушай" EDM song featuring the character goes up on YouTube and later passes 38 million views.

ul: Photo slideshows dropping Smurf Cat into everyday scenes, set to "we live, we love, we lie".
Writing "шайлушай" in comments as a nonsense chant, even by people who do not speak Russian.
Edits in other meme templates, such as relationship and "babe please stop" formats.
Remixes such as the 2023 "Шайлушай" EDM song and fan art of the blue creature.

body: Smurf Cat peaked in autumn 2023 and faded after October that year, but it stayed in the Gen Alpha meme canon and often appears beside John Pork and Skibidi Toilet. The image still belongs to its artist, Nate Hallinan, who made it as a Smurf, not a cat.

faq.a: Not officially. The art shows a realistic Smurf; its face just looks cat-like, so the internet called it Smurf Cat.
Nothing. It is a made-up word, though it sounds like the Russian "шалопай" (a little rascal).

faq.q: What song is used with Smurf Cat?
faq.a: Usually a remix of Alan Walker's "The Spectre", the source of the line "we live, we love, we lie".
